tasks.title: GL+month active rollups for Actual (DUB) and Budget
tasks.objective: Reduce both sides to one active row per (gl_code, month) BEFORE any join, so the later cross-object composition cannot fan out.
acceptance_criteria: a reproducible warehouse rollup reduces DUB actuals to (gl_code, month) as SUM(actual_net) over cost centres (WHERE plant='DUB'), and an active-budget rollup reduces the ACTIVE budget batch to (gl_code, month) as SUM(budget_amount)::numeric(18,2) with period aliased to month, each reflecting ONLY the active batch
the budget rollup preserves the set of cost_center (Budget Components) labels per (gl_code, month) key as informational (never a join key), and carries raw rollover_amount untouched with no measure

a demonstrated warehouse-DB test proves each rollup reflects only the active batch: a retained prior actuals/budget batch does not change the rollup, and a budget reload swaps the active batch without altering actuals

required_tests.id: the actual_by_gl_month view reduces DUB actuals to gl_code and month as SUM of actual_net over cost centres, filtered to plant DUB and inheriting the active-batch filter through actual_by_key_month with no direct ingest_batch predicate, and exposes a constant plant DUB column; the budget_by_gl_month view rolls the active budget batch up to gl_code and month via its own direct join to ingest_batch on source_kind budget and is_active as SUM of budget_amount with period aliased to month, each asserted by SQL shape including the numeric 18 2 cast and the group-by key

tasks.reviewer_focus: FIRST task of governed-joins: two READ-ONLY warehouse GL+month rollup views that reduce each ingested object to ONE active row per (gl_code, month) BEFORE any cross-object join (the join itself is task 2, composed-relation). NO new endpoint, grant, base table, or dependency. It EXTENDS the warehouse schema built in sap-ingestion; mirror the existing actual_by_key_month view EXACTLY (backend/src/warehouse/warehouse-schema.ts:117-134, a drizzle pgView; its DDL is emitted in backend/drizzle-warehouse/0000_*.sql). GROUNDING: actual_by_key_month is Plant+CostCenter+GL+month (SUM(debit-credit)); mis_budget (warehouse-schema.ts:86-115) has NO plant, its month column is `period` (month-truncated), cost_center is the MIS 'Budget Components' LABEL, unique grain (batch_id,format_id,period,line_id,gl_code,cost_center); ingest_batch (warehouse-schema.ts:23-46) has the partial-unique active pointer on (source_kind, period) WHERE is_active. Decisions 0004 (no pre-join beyond this governed layer), 0015 (warehouse snake_case), 0016 (gl_code+month within DUB; Budget-Components label informational; roll-over measure deferred but raw rollover_amount kept). VIEW 1 actual_by_gl_month: SELECT 'DUB'::text AS plant, gl_code, month, SUM(actual_net)::numeric(18,2) AS actual_net FROM actual_by_key_month WHERE plant='DUB' GROUP BY gl_code, month — reduce the existing gold view across cost centres for the single DUB plant (the fan-out fix: without it, joining Plant+CostCenter+GL+month to a GL+month budget repeats Budget per cost centre). HUMAN-decided seam (task-1 grill round): EXPOSE a constant plant='DUB' column so task 2 can inject/verify its Actual-side scope predicate against the rollup. NOTE the active-batch filter is INHERITED through actual_by_key_month (which already filters source_kind='actuals' AND is_active) — this view has NO direct ingest_batch predicate; do not duplicate the join. VIEW 2 budget_by_gl_month: SELECT b.gl_code, b.period AS month, SUM(b.budget_amount)::numeric(18,2) AS budget_net, SUM(b.rollover_amount)::numeric(18,2) AS rollover_net, array_agg(DISTINCT b.cost_center ORDER BY b.cost_center) AS budget_component_labels FROM mis_budget b JOIN ingest_batch bt ON bt.id=b.batch_id WHERE bt.source_kind='budget' AND bt.is_active GROUP BY b.gl_code, b.period — the active budget batch only via its OWN direct join to ingest_batch; cost_center is NEVER a GROUP BY/join key, only a DETERMINISTIC informational label SET (the ORDER BY inside array_agg is REQUIRED — Postgres gives no order otherwise, and provenance/golden fixtures need determinism); rollover_net is carried but exposed by NO measure (roll-over deferred). Add both as drizzle pgViews in warehouse-schema.ts and their CREATE VIEW DDL in a NEW migration backend/drizzle-warehouse/0002_gl_month_rollups.sql AND its journal entry in backend/drizzle-warehouse/meta/_journal.json (both are owned; a migration not in the journal will not apply on a clean warehouse), applied by `npm --prefix backend run warehouse:migrate` (follow how 0000/0001 are wired). HERMETIC TESTS (warehouse-schema.test.ts, in test:hermetic): assert each view's SQL shape (active-batch filter, the (gl_code, month) GROUP BY, numeric(18,2) casts, DUB filter on actuals, the label-set aggregate, rollover carried) — regex/string assertions like the existing actual_by_key_month tests, no DB. D-0008 GATED PROOF (a NEW backend/src/warehouse/gl-month-rollups.db.test.ts, `{ skip: process.env.WAREHOUSE_DB_TEST !== '1' }`): migrateWarehouse(), then use IngestionRepository (NOT direct SQL inserts — the proof must exercise the atomic candidate-load-then-flip active-batch invariant) to: (a) load a PRIOR actuals batch then a REPLACEMENT actuals batch (across MULTIPLE cost centres for one gl_code+month in DUB) and assert the prior stays inactive, ONLY the replacement contributes, and actual_by_gl_month sums the replacement's cost centres to ONE row (with plant='DUB'); (b) load a PRIOR budget batch then a REPLACEMENT budget batch and assert budget_by_gl_month reflects ONLY the active batch and exposes the deterministic label set; (c) a budget reload swaps the active budget batch WITHOUT changing actuals. Guard the destructive TRUNCATE to loopback-only hosts and add a dead-port negative control. REGISTRATION (every backend *.test.ts is in EXACTLY ONE declared hermetic suite): add gl-month-rollups.db.test.ts to test:hermetic AND its hermeticTests registry in tools/quality-gate.test.mjs (the gated leaf self-skips there). RUNNABLE PROOF: EXTEND the existing backend/package.json `test:warehouse-proof` script (which today runs ONLY reconciliation.repository.test.ts) to run BOTH proofs — RETAIN reconciliation.repository.test.ts and add this file — and because both destructively TRUNCATE shared warehouse tables they MUST run SERIALIZED (node --test with --test-concurrency=1, or a sequential invocation), so one proof never wipes the other mid-run. Commit tests.json with the pinned host command (`... WAREHOUSE_DB_TEST=1 npm --prefix backend run test:warehouse-proof`, TS_NODE_PROJECT retained) + pass counts + the dead-port negative control (per decision 0009 + the sap-ingestion D-0008 lessons: demonstrated host evidence run by the orchestrator; the evidence record must be COMMITTED into the diff BEFORE review). NEVER read/write/join across the two objects here (that is task 2).

review_budget.reason: Two read-only warehouse GL+month rollup views (a DUB actual reduction + an active-budget rollup preserving the Budget-Components label set) mirroring actual_by_key_month, their migration, hermetic SQL-shape tests, and a WAREHOUSE_DB_TEST=1 gated proof that each reflects only the active batch and the actual reduction does not repeat across cost centres. No endpoint, grant, base table, or dependency.

tasks.title: Closed, typed, code-composed Budget⋈Actual relation with two-sided scope
tasks.objective: Provide ONE governed financial gold relation that full-outer-joins the two GL+month rollups with zero-fill, serves every gold-object consumer, and enforces role-based access with the scope predicate inside both source CTEs.
acceptance_criteria: a single closed, typed, code-composed financial relation full-outer-joins the two GL+month rollup views on gl_code and month with COALESCE zero-fill so a budget-only key and an actual-only key both appear, replacing the SQL builder's multi-gold-object rejection, and returns objectsTouched listing both source view leaf names for the validator allow-list; freshness, dimension enumeration and RBAC scope-validation stay pointed at the real source views and composed reconciliation is deferred (the governed measures are kept non-critical), with a revisit trigger for multi-plant/production

a governed-financial read action is required at the shared SelectionExecutor execution boundary together with the domain and Actual/Budget/% grants, and the row-scope predicate is injected INSIDE each source CTE before the join (Actual by plant, Budget by its trusted derived constant DUB); a denial case and a predicate-placement test are included
a demonstrated warehouse-DB test proves the composed relation zero-fills correctly and does NOT fan out: a GL with multiple actual cost centres does not repeat Budget, and totals are exact

required_tests.id: the SQL builder composes a governed financial relation as WITH aliased actual and budget CTEs that select from the real rollup views and are full outer joined on gl_code and month, with COALESCE zero-fill in the relation so an all-budget-only key yields actual_net 0 and an all-actual-only key yields budget_net 0, instead of throwing the multi gold object error, and returns objectsTouched listing both source view leaf names

the row-scope constraint is applied INSIDE each source CTE and not on the outer query: the Actual CTE filters its plant column to DUB against the user validated scope and the Budget CTE is structurally DUB by construction with no plant predicate, asserted on the composed SQL text, and the CTE aliases differ from the view names so no view is shadowed

the composed WITH full-outer-join query passes sqlValidator when the two source view leaf names AND the builder deterministic CTE alias names are all in the allowed objects, and is rejected when a source view leaf is removed from the allow-list, proving the base view allow-list is the enforced security check while the code-fixed CTE alias names are not a data-source bypass

the selection executor enforces authorization at the shared executeResolved boundary for a governed financial domain: it throws a fail-closed error when the user lacks the governed financial read action, OR lacks the domain grant, OR lacks a grant for any selected measure or dimension, and allows a user holding the read action plus the domain and all selected measure and dimension grants

tasks.reviewer_focus: SECOND governed-joins task: ONE closed, typed, code-composed financial relation that full-outer-joins the two GL+month rollup views from task 1 (actual_by_gl_month, budget_by_gl_month, backend/src/warehouse/warehouse-schema.ts) on (gl_code, month) with COALESCE zero-fill, replacing the SQL builder's multi-gold-object rejection, plus a governed-financial READ action enforced (with the domain + selected measure/dimension grants) at the shared execution boundary. NARROWED SCOPE (grill round + 0016): the composed relation is the JOIN that measure QUERIES run; freshness / dimension enumeration / RBAC scope-validation STAY pointed at the real source views and composed reconciliation is DEFERRED (governed measures kept non-critical) - do NOT rework those consumers here. NO new warehouse object; NO measures or domain in baseDomains (task 3); NO endpoint. Decisions 0004, 0016, 0009. COMPOSED MARKER: add a BUILDER-ONLY optional typed field to DomainSpec (contract/src/measure.ts) - e.g. `composed?: { sources: string[]; joinKeys: string[] }` naming the two source views + ['gl_code','month'] - while goldObject/freshnessColumn/scopeColumn still point at a REAL source view (actual_by_gl_month) so the deferred consumers keep working unchanged. BUILDER (sqlBuilder.ts): BRANCH before the multi-gold-object throw at lines 29-32 when the domain carries the composed marker. Emit `WITH a AS (SELECT gl_code, month, actual_net FROM actual_by_gl_month WHERE plant IN (:scope)), b AS (SELECT gl_code, month, budget_net, rollover_net, budget_component_labels FROM budget_by_gl_month) SELECT COALESCE(a.gl_code,b.gl_code) AS gl_code, COALESCE(a.month,b.month) AS month, COALESCE(a.actual_net,0) AS actual_net, COALESCE(b.budget_net,0) AS budget_net, ... FROM a FULL OUTER JOIN b ON a.gl_code=b.gl_code AND a.month=b.month ... LIMIT :max`. CRITICAL FIXES from the grill: (1) the CTE ALIASES (a, b or actual_src/budget_src) MUST DIFFER from the view names - naming a CTE after the view it selects from SELF-SHADOWS (a recursive self-reference) and will not run; (2) budget_by_gl_month HAS NO plant column, so the Budget CTE takes NO plant predicate - Budget is structurally DUB-only by construction (0016 single plant); the two-sided scope is Actual filtered by its plant='DUB' column against the user's validated scope + Budget inherently DUB. ZERO-FILL OWNERSHIP (grill finding 3): the two rollup views are ALREADY one row per (gl_code, month), so the composed relation is a 1:1 full-outer join with NO re-aggregation; the COALESCE zero-fill of actual_net / budget_net (and the coalesced join keys) is OWNED HERE (task 2), so task-3 measures reference already-0-filled columns and never see NULL. Return objectsTouched = ['actual_by_gl_month','budget_by_gl_month']. VALIDATOR (sqlValidator.ts is NOT in write_scope - do not edit it): the composed WITH query must PASS the existing validator. CONFIRMED: node-sql-parser tableList INCLUDES the CTE alias names (a/b), not only the base views. RESOLUTION (no validator edit): the composed builder - which controls BOTH the SQL and objectsTouched - returns objectsTouched = the two base view leaves PLUS its own deterministic CTE alias names, so the unchanged validator passes. The base views remain the enforced allow-list: any UNAPPROVED base table (e.g. sap_transaction) is still rejected because the builder never adds it; the CTE alias names are code-fixed internal references, not a data-source bypass. Cover in sqlValidator.composed.test.ts: the composed query PASSES with the two view leaves + the alias names allow-listed, and is REJECTED when a base VIEW leaf is removed. Put the LIMIT on the outer SELECT. GOVERNED-READ ACTION + BOUNDARY ENFORCEMENT (t-cr-c2, grill findings 4+5): add ONE new action to GRANT_ACTIONS in grants.constants.ts (a governed-financial read action, e.g. 'report'). Task 2 SEEDS ONLY the ACTION grant to role 'admin' in backend/src/db/migrate.ts baseRolePerms (mirror {role:'admin',grantType:'action',grantId:'ingest'}, onConflictDoNothing) and UPDATES backend/src/db/migrate.test.ts for it - the governed-financial domain/measure/dimension grants are TASK 3's (they arrive WITH the domain). ENFORCE at the SHARED chokepoint in selectionExecutor.ts executeResolved (before builder.build ~line 94): for a governed-financial / composed domain, require ALL of - user.permissions.actions includes the read action, the domain grant, and a grant for EVERY selected measure and dimension - else throw a fail-closed SelectionExecutionBlockedError (allowedFor only filters metadata; the executor accepts a supplied domain/selection directly, so a user with the action but without the domain/measure grant must still be denied here). Test all denial branches with a FIXTURE governed-financial composed domain (task 2 has no real domain; use a fixture like definitionVersion.test.ts). HERMETIC TESTS (test:hermetic, NEW files): sqlBuilder.composed.test.ts (composed WITH/FULL OUTER JOIN/COALESCE shape, aliases differ from views, scope inside the Actual CTE only, objectsTouched both leaves); sqlValidator.composed.test.ts (allow-list pass/reject); selectionExecutor.composed.test.ts (each authorization denial branch + the granted-allow case, fixture domain, fake Warehouse). D-0008 GATED PROOF (NEW backend/src/warehouse/composed-relation.db.test.ts, { skip: WAREHOUSE_DB_TEST !== '1' }): migrateWarehouse(), seed via IngestionRepository actual+budget batches with a matched (gl,month) key, a Budget-only key, an Actual-only key, and a multi-cost-centre actual GL; run the composed builder's SQL through the read-only Warehouse and assert exact values: matched row nets both sides, Budget-only zero-fills actual, Actual-only zero-fills budget, multi-cost-centre GL does NOT repeat Budget (no fan-out). Guard the destructive TRUNCATE to loopback-only hosts; dead-port negative control; EXTEND backend/package.json test:warehouse-proof to run it serialized (--test-concurrency=1) with the existing reconciliation + gl-month-rollups proofs; register in test:hermetic + hermeticTests (tools/quality-gate.test.mjs). Commit tests.json with the pinned host command + pass counts + negative control BEFORE review (the review bundle EXCLUDES .factory, so the runnable test:warehouse-proof command in package.json is the reviewer-visible D-0008 proof). NEVER author the join in the LLM/runtime - code-composed only (0004). Keep required_test ids regex-metacharacter-free and name each test() leaf verbatim (task-1 D-0024 lesson).

review_budget.reason: The core cross-object capability: a composed-marker on DomainSpec, the code-composed full-outer zero-filled Budget-Actual join in the SQL builder (replacing the multi-gold-object throw, aliased CTEs, COALESCE zero-fill owned here, in-CTE Actual scope, both-leaf objectsTouched), a governed-financial read action + boundary enforcement of action+domain+measure+dimension grants (+ its seed and migrate.test update), hermetic builder/validator/executor-denial tests, and a gated D-0008 zero-fill/no-fan-out proof. Freshness/enum/scope-validation stay per-view; reconciliation deferred.

tasks.title: Code-authored Actual / Budget / % measures over the composed relation
tasks.objective: Author the governed financial domain and its measures in code so report, drill-down and assistant share one definition; the LLM only selects measures.
acceptance_criteria: a code-authored financial DomainSpec and Actual (SUM(Debit-Credit)), Budget (SUM(budget_amount)) and % MeasureSpecs are registered in semanticLayer baseDomains over the composed relation; two-column expressions are code-authored (not the runtime builder), and the LLM/runtime never authors the SQL

% follows the full nil rule: 0/0 -> NA/blank; Actual>0,Budget=0 -> over-budget (no %); Actual<0,Budget=0 -> credit / negative actual (no %); i.e. no percentage for any non-zero Actual against zero Budget, with the positive/negative labels distinguished

tasks.title: Golden-answer fixtures (no fan-out) + provenance lineage
tasks.objective: Gate correctness with exact golden fixtures and make every governed number reproducible and explainable.
acceptance_criteria: a golden-answer reconciliation fixture asserts EXACT expected values for matched, Budget-only (zero-filled), Actual-only (zero-filled), duplicate/multi-cost-centre (no fan-out), reload/active-swap (answer unchanged, actuals untouched), and %-edge (0/0 NA, positive over-budget, negative credit/negative-actual) cases, as demonstrated host evidence (D-0008)

provenance for every governed number carries the measure definition + composed SQL PLUS active source batch ids keyed by (source, period), row-aligned source-presence (matched / budget-only / actual-only, or a set for aggregate rows), and a deterministic set of Budget-Components labels, all captured within the same composed query
